soundcheck.heard: What if moving cook inlet power means moving the computer instead? Deep Green proposes 66 compute hives near Nikiski. Around them, 330 to 350 marine hydrokinetic turbines. The turbines would power them directly while seawater provides passive cooling. Clever, put the primary load beside its proposed power source. A 3.5 mile cable would carry power and fiber ashore. The notice estimates 100 megawatts. Where would it go? The data center would be the primary use. Only spare power could reach the rail belt. Could, not will. Now put that diagram on a test bench. The filing names no customer or committed financing. No completed proof covers output, cooling, economics, grid connection or environmental effects. That doesn't make it bad. It makes the next step a study. On September 4th, FERC opened public comment on the application. If issued, the permit gives study priority. It wouldn't authorize construction or prove that one turbine works there. Comments and competing applications are due November 2nd at 1pm Alaska time. Brief comments need no prior registration. So stop the cable one inch short of victory. Bringing compute to cook inlet energy is the clever part. It becomes an Alaska win when studies prove engineering, grid, economics and environmental effects. What would you require?
